topic.title: Fastest reply wins
topic.claim: In most offices the person who replies in ten seconds gets promoted over the person who did the actual work.
topic.moment: The green dot on Teams that someone keeps alive while doing nothing.

turn.actually: Managers can't see work, only replies, so speed on chat gets read as commitment.

topic.because: A manager with eight reports judges by what shows up on their screen. A quick 'on it' feels like ownership even when nothing follows.
topic.payoff: Count how often your manager has seen your work versus your replies. That ratio is your review.
topic.behaviour: People keep chat open all day, answer instantly and do deep work after hours.
topic.mechanism: Visibility is cheap to judge and output is hard to judge, so visibility wins.
topic.group: Corporate employees who do slow, careful work
topic.send_to: The quiet colleague who does the hardest work and gets the 'meets expectations' rating.
topic.why_now: Hybrid work made chat the main way managers see their team at all.

score.why: Managers see replies, not work, so the green-dot person gets promoted; very relatable office truth.

topic.villain: a visibility gap where managers reward replies they can see over work they can't
